name: Active Minds
description: Student-led mental health awareness and advocacy organization. Chapters on college campuses nationwide.

sections.title: About Active Minds
sections.text: Active Minds is the nation's premier nonprofit organization supporting mental health awareness and education for young adults. Founded in 2003, Active Minds empowers students to speak openly about mental health to reduce stigma and create lasting change on college campuses. The organization has chapters at over 1,000 high schools, colleges, and universities across the United States and internationally.

sections.title: Campus Chapters
sections.text: Active Minds chapters are student-led groups that promote mental health awareness through campus events, peer education, and advocacy initiatives. Chapters host events like Send Silence Packing (a traveling exhibit on suicide awareness), stress relief activities during finals, and discussions about mental health. Students can start a new chapter at their school or join an existing one.

sections.title: Programs and Initiatives
sections.text: Active Minds offers training programs including Mental Health First Aid, gatekeeper training for identifying students in distress, and leadership development for chapter officers. The organization runs awareness campaigns like Active Minds Week, provides curriculum for mental health education, and advocates for policies that support student mental health on campus and nationally.

sections.title: Resources for Students
sections.text: Active Minds provides free resources for students including guides on finding campus mental health services, information about common mental health challenges in college, tips for supporting friends in distress, and self-care strategies. The website includes personal stories from students who have faced mental health challenges and found support through Active Minds.

sections.title: How to Get Involved
sections.text: Students can get involved with Active Minds by joining a local chapter, starting a new chapter at their school, participating in campus events, or becoming a Send Silence Packing volunteer. The organization also offers internships, leadership programs, and opportunities to share your story to help reduce mental health stigma among young people.
